Worked Example: 200 lb for 5 Reps

If you lift 200 lb for 5 clean reps, the Epley formula (weight × (1 + reps ÷ 30)) gives an estimated one rep max of 233 lb. The Brzycki formula (weight × 36 ÷ (37 − reps)) gives 225 lb. Estimates differ by a few percent, and all are most reliable at 10 reps or fewer.

Turning 1RM Into a Training Plan

% of 1RMWeight (using 233 lb)Typical use
85%198 lbHeavy sets, strength
75%175 lbModerate sets, 8-10 reps
65%152 lbHigher reps, endurance

Safety

  • Estimating is safer than testing a true one-rep max, especially without a spotter.
  • Use sets you completed with good form; a grinding last rep skews the estimate.
  • Recalculate every few weeks as you get stronger.

Pair training with enough protein; see the protein calculator.

extra_faqs.q: Which one rep max formula is the most accurate?
extra_faqs.a: No single formula is best for everyone. Epley and Brzycki are widely used and close to each other at low reps. Use the same formula consistently to track progress.

extra_faqs.q: Is it safe to test a true 1RM?
extra_faqs.a: It carries more risk than submaximal sets. Use a spotter or safety bars and warm up thoroughly, or estimate from a lighter set instead.
Yes, but form should come first. Estimates are less stable when technique is still changing.
